chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Musa ibn Abd al-Malik and al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from Musa ibn Abd al-Malik from a man who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man coming to his wife from behind in her rear [anus], so he said: 'It was made permissible by a verse from the Book of Allah, the Exalted: The saying of Lut (peace be upon him),
These are my daughters, they are purer for you,
and He knew that they did not desire the vagina.'

key_terms.إِتْيَانُ الرَّجُلِ الْمَرْأَةَ: A man coming to his wife (sexual intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic evidence for the permissibility of anal intercourse with one's wife in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) derives the permissibility of vaginal intercourse from behind by interpreting the phrase 'These are my daughters' in the story of Prophet Lut (AS) as a reference to the vagina, which he deems 'purer' for sexual use. This juristic reasoning hinges on the premise that God’s knowledge of the men's specific desire for the vagina implies that the term 'daughters' was used metonymically to distinguish the vaginal canal from other orifices, thereby validating the act despite its unconventional position.
